identity.title: Nonnegative Cross-Curvature in Infinite Dimensions: Synthetic Definition and Spaces of Measures
identity.version: arXiv:2409.18112v3, 9 November 2025, internal date 11 November 2025; exact 52-page packet PDF

assessment: Major revision required: the random-variable lifting statement is false under its printed assumptions, and the general measurable-selection proof and two advertised examples require substantive correction.
outcome: Four confirmed Major and nine confirmed Minor findings; exact-source initial scientific review complete. Independent scientific acceptance remains pending.

problems.title: Proposition 3.17: expected-cost NNCC fails without intermediate integrability
problems.assumptions: X=Y=R,c(x,y)=4^x sin^2(pi x)+(x-y)^2; discrete atoms p_k=2^-k, T0=k,T1=k+1,Sbar=k. All printed hypotheses and finite endpoint costs0,1 hold.
problems.decisive_evidence: One-atom target variations force T_s(k)=k+s; midpoint expected cost has partial sums 2^(N+2)-4+(1-2^-N)/4 and diverges.
problems.impact: Stated random-variable/infinite-product stability proposition is false; main Theorem3.7 including3.5 is not refuted.
problems.repair_limit: Add measurable selection and verified integrable intermediate-cost control;3.5 can address integrability but not repair P2.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Definition2.6 p.9 requires finite base cost at every time; Proposition3.17 pp.25-26 has Polish/lower-semicontinuous/bounded-below assumptions and does not invoke3.5.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: c=4^x sin^2(pi x)+(x-y)^2 is finite smooth nonnegative and NNCC by cancellation along affine x. Atomic probabilities2^-k sum1. T0=k,T1=k+1,Sbar=k have expected costs0,1. Single-atom changes of target preserve finiteness whenever an admissible intermediate base cost is finite.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Both signs of an arbitrary single-atom target variation force Ts(k)=k+s. At s=1/2 the first N base-cost terms equal2^(N+2)-4+(1-2^-N)/4, diverging. Thus no admissible midpoint exists.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: inf_y c(x,y)=4^x sin^2(pi x) is unbounded, violating3.5. Theorem3.7 and the metric specialization are not refuted by this example. Pointwise cancellation cannot define infinity minus infinity after expectation.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False stated infinite-product/random-variable stability proposition; Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Require genuine measurable intermediate selections and verified integrable base-cost control; adding3.5 does not itself resolve P2.

problems.title: Lemma 3.3: false graph inclusion in measurable selection
problems.assumptions: Quadratic cost on R, gamma=delta_(0,2,0),s=1/2,c_n=c,Z_k^1=Z_k^2={(0,0),(2,0)} satisfy all compact-set and convergence prerequisites.
problems.decisive_evidence: Unique midpoint1 gives (0,2,0,1) in Graph intersect Ztilde but not any F_k,n,m since (1,0) not in Z_k.
problems.impact: Core existence-of-lift proof and general Polish-space lifting theorem lack this dependency; no counterexample to the lemma conclusion asserted.
problems.repair_limit: Replace selection argument and justify common-full-set/all-time quantifiers; no complete general repair certified.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Lemma3.3 p.22; full proof pp.47-48, (B.13)-(B.15). Definition3.2 quantifies a common full set for the selected path.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Quadratic cost, gamma=delta_(0,2,0),s=1/2,cn=c, all Zk1=Zk2={(0,0),(2,0)} satisfy endpoint mass-one compactness and uniform approximation requirements.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Unique variational midpoint1 is in Graph(Lambda_tilde) intersect Ztilde, but no Fk,n,m contains it because (1,0) is absent from Zk. This failure is on the whole gamma mass for every n,m. Endpoint-controlled sets do not control an unknown midpoint or all comparison targets.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The same witness has an obvious measurable affine selector; it refutes the printed graph reconstruction, not the lemma's conclusion. A common Lusin set only repairs the separate endpoint-intersection error.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Lemma3.4 and Theorem3.7 explicitly depend on3.3. A demonstrated false core derivation step supports Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: No general replacement selection proof is supplied; all-time/common-full-set quantifiers must be retained.

problems.title: Example 3.21 fails its global LMP base hypothesis
problems.assumptions: Printed base c=-log|x-y| off diagonal; horizontal endpoints(-1,0),(1,0) and base(-1/2,0) have finite costs.
problems.decisive_evidence: LMP first variations force continuous gradient into segment[-2,2/3]e1; it must cross0 although (x-y)/|x-y|^2 never vanishes. Figure midpoint ratio289/225>1 is separately correct.
problems.impact: Example does not prove non-preservation from a global LMP base; compact smooth converse hypotheses also not verified for this noncompact singular cost.
problems.repair_limit: Provide a genuine LMP Cartesian base and applicable lifting necessity; no other non-lifting example disproved.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Global continuous LMP definition pp.10,18; Example3.21 pp.28-29; compact smooth twisted LemmasB.9-B.11 pp.44-46.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Horizontal endpoints(-1,0),(1,0),base(-1/2,0) are finite-cost pairs. Target variations near the base are legitimate in both signs for every finite candidate point.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: First variations force the continuous gradient (x-ybar)/|x-ybar|^2 into[-2,2/3]e1, joining its endpoints. The intermediate value theorem forces zero, impossible for finite off-diagonal x. Figure midpoint ratios17/5 and17/45 still give a positive quarter-log(289/225).
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Correct failure of those particular lifted curves does not give a counterexample to preservation from a global LMP base. A smooth off-diagonal non-Cartesian locus does not meet the global base claim; the compact converse cannot silently be applied to this singular noncompact cost.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The advertised non-preservation example lacks its required premise; Major for that claimed result.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Another valid global base/example may exist; none is ruled out or supplied here.

problems.title: WFR sphere argument conflates entropy and Euclidean cone costs
problems.assumptions: KL perspective minimizes at z=sqrt(rs)e^-c/2; sphere antipodes r=s1 permitted.
problems.decisive_evidence: Printed entropy cost gives0, signed cone formula4, genuine HK squared2. With Euclidean cone and prescribed target unit lift every source lift costs2+2E sqrt(r)>2; inf2 not attained.
problems.impact: Literal WFR metric formula false and Euclidean-cone cost-submersion deduction invalid; corrected WFR NNCC not refuted.
problems.repair_limit: Distinguish pi/2 entropy perspective from pi Euclidean cone; retain tip reservoir and prove an appropriate replacement lifting argument.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: (4.19),(4.22),Lemma4.19 pp.35-36, Theorem4.20/Example4.21 p.37 and proof pp.48-49; retained primary reference pp.85,92-95,100.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For KL and positive r,s, strictly convex objective has z=sqrt(rs)e^-c/2. Antipodes on unit sphere and unit masses are allowed. Manuscript uses mass radius; primary reference uses its square root.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Perspective minimum is r+s-2sqrt(rs)e^-c/2. Printed squared cosine gives absolute cosine, so antipodal value0 contradicts displayed4 and gives zero literal ET cost for distinct Diracs. Correct ET cutoffpi/2 gives squared HK2. For the Euclidean cone with target lift delta_(y,1), every probability source lift has E r=1 and cost2+2E sqrt(r)>2. Epsilon at r=1/epsilon and rest at tip approaches2 but never attains it.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The primary reference distinguishes pi andpi/2 truncations and retains a tip reservoir in its normalization. Existence of suitable common lifts is not attainment for every prescribed lift. This does not disprove correctly defined WFR NNCC; the nonnegative-cosine PSD example avoids this specific obstruction.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Pointwise formula contradiction plus failure of the fixed-lift cost-submersion route used for the sphere, Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: A new justified sphere deduction and correct lifting/integrability hypotheses are required; cosmetic cutoff/sign edits alone do not supply them.

problems.title: Bi-twist implication and signed quotient in differential preliminaries
problems.assumptions: c=x^3y+xy^3 is smooth bi-twisted with convex gradient images; separately c=-x^2y^2,x(s)=s,base0 satisfies Lemma2.5 inequality.
problems.decisive_evidence: Mixed derivative vanishes at origin in first example. At s1/2,t=-1 displayed quotient inequality is -1/4<=-1/2, false.
problems.impact: Incorrect preliminary implication and intermediate inequality; Theorem2.4 and Lemma2.5 conclusions not refuted.
problems.repair_limit: Retain nondegeneracy independently; use t down to0 or Fermat gap derivative.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Claim before Definition2.2 and quotient inequality(2.10), p.8.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: c=x^3y+xy^3 is C-infinity, bi-twisted with full convex gradient images. Separately c=-x^2y^2,x(s)=s,ybar=0 meets the lemma's smooth-path inequality.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: cxy(0,0)=0 in the first example. In the second, s=1/2,t=-1 turns the quotient assertion into -1/4<=-1/2, false.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Theorem2.4 independently includes nondegeneracy. Lemma2.5's conclusion follows from t down to0 with arbitrary signed tangent, or the derivative of the comparison gap at its minimum.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Two local preliminary errors with explicit valid repair, Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Retain nondegeneracy separately and restrict the signed division correctly.

problems.title: Negative gravity exits the domain in Example 2.11
problems.decisive_evidence: First target derivatives force midpoint(0,-7), outside a>0.
problems.impact: NNCC example false for permitted negative g.
problems.repair_limit: Require g>0; positive gravity makes displayed a(s)>0 and affine differences.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Example2.11 p.11 explicitly allows every nonzero real g.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: g=-1,H=R,endpoints(-4,1),(4,1),base(0,1) are in the domain with costs7.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: First derivatives in target y and b force the midpoint x=0,a=-7, outside a>0. No continuity assumption on the candidate path is needed.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: For g>0 the displayed correction to a(s) is nonnegative, preserving the domain and making the cost differences affine.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False extra parameter range in a local example, Minor.

problems.title: Projection remarks omit continuity and common-map requirements
problems.assumptions: Singleton-fiber identity projections into discrete first target; separately P1=id,P2(y)=y+1 with squared Euclidean cost.
problems.decisive_evidence: No continuous path0 to1 in discrete target; shifted projected distance has diagonal1 and distinct zero.
problems.impact: LMP and metric conclusions need extra compatibility, algebraic NNCC submersion remains unaffected.
problems.repair_limit: Require continuous first projection for LMP and common quotient map for metric conclusion.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Definition2.17 p.12 only imposes surjective set maps/cost attainment; Remarks2.21-2.22 p.14 add LMP/metric conclusions.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Quadratic cost with identity set maps from usual real line to a discrete first target meets all algebraic singleton-fiber requirements. Independently P1=id,P2(y)=y+1 meets the same requirements.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The discrete target has no continuous path0 to1 despite upstairs LMP. Shifted projected root cost |u-v+1| has diagonal value1 and vanishes for distinct points.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The algebraic NNCC proposition does not need continuity. A continuous first projection repairs LMP; a common quotient map and the attained lifting equalities give the metric axioms.

problems.repair_limit: Use actual compact domains and properness or retain explicit support assumptions.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Theorem2.35 open bounded-domain assumptions and following attainment statement(2.40), p.20; c-transform definitions p.19.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: X=Y=(0,1),c=-xy,psi=-x meet C4, twist, nondegeneracy, convex images and continuous extension to compact closure.

problems.title: Matrix metric normalization, logarithm range and Gaussian completeness
problems.assumptions: Scalar matrices1,e,e^2; logI=0; offdiagonal variation at diag(4,1); variance path(1-t)^2.
problems.decisive_evidence: Printed norm gives triangle4>1+1. Log maps to Sym. Congruence coefficients log4/3<1/2 differ. Positive variance reaches0 at finite length.
problems.impact: Local metric descriptions false literally; corrected log-Euclidean and Bures examples remain supported.
problems.repair_limit: Insert square root, use Sym as log image, distinguish affine-invariant metric, replace complete by convex and include PSD completion.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Log metric and Frobenius definition p.25; repeated norm and Gaussian completeness p.34.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Scalar positive matrices1,e,e^2; off-diagonal symmetric variation at diag(4,1); positive variance(1-t)^2 for0<=t<1.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Printed norm yields triangle4>1+1. logI=0 and exp maps every symmetric matrix to PD. Off-diagonal logarithmic coefficientlog4/3 differs from congruence coefficient1/2. BW along the variance path equals|t-u| and reaches the excluded zero variance at finite length.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The corrected log-Euclidean space is Hilbert under log; proper Frobenius quotient proves the intended PSD theorem. Nondegenerate Gaussians are geodesically convex, not complete.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Insert the square root, use all symmetric matrices as logarithm image, distinguish affine invariance, and include PSD for completion.

problems.title: Right inverse does not exist in singular polar-factor formula
problems.decisive_evidence: Zero has no right inverse; pseudoinverse gives U=0 and wrong endpoint covariance.
problems.impact: Displayed segment formula undefined at advertised boundary; existence theorem not refuted.
problems.repair_limit: Use orthogonal polar-factor completion on kernels; inverse formula only when invertible.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Proposition4.12 and its proof pp.34-35 permit singular PSD matrices while demanding a right inverse.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Zero admits no right inverse. A Moore-Penrose substitution gives U=0, not orthogonal, and the wrong endpoint covariance.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Choose an orthogonal completion in the polar factorization sqrt(S2)sqrt(Si)=Ui sqrt(sqrt(Si)S2sqrt(Si)); Mi=sqrt(Si)Ui^T has correct covariance and optimal trace alignment.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Boundary formula defect with explicit repair; Theorem4.10 existence is not refuted. Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use orthogonal polar factors on kernels; inverse formula only in the invertible case.

problems.title: Fisher-Rao formula omits Hellinger square
problems.assumptions: Disjoint unit Diracs have H^2=2 and orthogonal square-root densities.
problems.decisive_evidence: Printed acos(1-sqrt2/2)<pi/2, while spherical angle pi/2.
problems.impact: Displayed normalization inconsistent with its own definition and proof.

independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Disjoint unit Diracs are probability measures and have orthogonal unit square-root densities.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: H=sqrt2 and spherical distancepi/2; printed arccos(1-H/2) gives a strictly smaller value.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The subsequent spherical argument applies to arccos(1-H^2/2), with the paper's normalization.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Missing square in a local displayed identity, Minor.

problems.title: Partial-transport cone formula has the wrong minimum
problems.repair_limit: Use r+s-min(r,s)max(0,2-d^q) as c_C, without unexplained extra outer q-power.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Partial-transport example p.36 compared with definition(4.19).
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: F=|t-1|,q>=1,c=d^q>=0,r,s>0. The infimum over positive z has the same value as z>=0 by continuity at zero.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Piecewise-linear minimization gives r+s-min(r,s)max(0,2-d^q). r=s=1,d=0,q=1 gives0, whereas the printed minimum gives2.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This is a local example formula and does not by itself refute the general conic formulation.

limitations: The refuted statement is Proposition 3.17 under its printed assumptions; its counterexample does not satisfy (3.5) and does not refute Theorem 3.7.
The Lemma 3.3 compact-set graph argument fails, but its conclusion is not disproved by the quadratic-cost witness; a general repaired selection theorem is not supplied.
The global negative-log example lacks its asserted base-space LMP. This does not prove that no other LMP non-preservation example exists.
The WFR argument conflates entropy and cone costs and arbitrary fixed-lift attainment. Correct WFR/HK nonnegative cross-curvature is not refuted; no replacement proof is claimed.
Only exact arXiv v3 was reviewed; equivalence to the journal version is not asserted.
Relevant sections of one primary 2018 reference were read; its entire 149-page text and all other cited proofs were not newly audited.
No author code was executed. Missing code is not counted as a mathematical defect.
UI attribution is the controller's observation; the runtime is GPT-6 Astra Pro, with no independent claim of backend equivalence.
repair_verification: Each local correction is checked in the English report. Integrable domination does not by itself settle measurable selection. The quadratic compact-set counterexample, the global LMP obstruction and the antipodal fixed-lift obstruction are separated from unproved claims about corrected main theorems. No whole-paper acceptance or universal repair is asserted.
independent_acceptance_scope: Focused verification of every P1-P13 in the exact acquired 52-page arXiv v3, including defining hypotheses, core dependencies and explicit local repairs. No complete second source review; no journal equivalence. Historical initial full-reading and broader reference claims remain historically attributed.
